newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends steady, cracks widen on weak Brent.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends steady, cracks widen on weak Brent.

text.p: IPE gas oil ended Monday unchanged, while weaker Brent futures pushed out the crack spread, a rough indicator of refining margins, brokers said.
April gas oil closed at $170.75 a tonne, while May Brent was trading 19 cents down at $19.80 a barrel at 1755 GMT. The May Brent/gas oil crack spread was trading at $3.29 a barrel.
"There's no real strength in gas oil, it's just Brent is ultra weak," said one broker.
Brokers said that a well supplied physical Brent market in Europe, and intermonth spreads trading in contango on the cash Brent market were keeping up the pressure on futures.
"The spreads on Brent got hammered all day," a broker said.
Brokers Prudential Bache said in their daily report that a break of support at $19.70/75 for Brent and $21.50/25 for NYMEX crude would imply a break of 30-40 cents lower.
"The physical glut in Europe, illustrated by the discount on Dated Brent, continues to weigh on the market," the report said.
Weak fundamentals eclipsed any bullish impact of disruptions to crude production in Nigeria, dealers said.
Shell Nigeria said a dispute between rival villagers caused the weekend shutdown of five pumping stations which cut output through the Forcados crude export system by 100,000 bpd.
But traders said that that a supply cushion of 1.8 million barrels of Forcados held by Shell should shield against disruptions to exports.
A spokesman for the company said it would be able to meet all of its March export commitments.
